topic: Leaked secret in git: rotate first, because rewriting history doesn't undo the exposure (GitHub docs)
text:
You pushed an API key to GitHub. Deleting the commit doesn't fix it. 🔑

GitHub's own guide says it plainly: for a secret, you need to revoke and/or rotate it. Rewriting history comes second, and it may not be needed once the key is dead.

Why history rewriting isn't a cleanup:
• Forks keep the commit, and you can't clean other people's clones
• Old clones can push the secret back
• Cached views and PR refs can still serve the commit after a force-push
• Commit hashes change, which breaks tooling and signatures

My order: 1) revoke and issue a new key, 2) check the provider's logs for use of the old one, 3) only then decide on a rewrite. Then turn on push protection so it can't happen again.

What's the first thing on your team's checklist when a key leaks?

image.alt: Four-step checklist for a leaked secret: rotate, check logs, decide on rewrite, prevent repeats, signed Ali Hassan, alihexan.com
